open_points.subject: Project anonymisation
open_points.text: R0-62 says an anonymised project keeps "its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else", while M01 says it also keeps "the anonymised mark" and calls that "exactly what R0-62 says".
open_points.question: Is anonymisation represented by a stored Project fact, or inferred from an archived record having only the retained facts?
options: Store an explicit anonymised mark in addition to id, status and pointers
Store no mark and infer anonymisation from the reduced record
Amend State 0 so the mark is expressly among the retained facts
open_points.default_guess: Store an explicit anonymised mark because later anonymisation and deletion behavior must distinguish it from an ordinary archived project.

open_points.subject: Confirmation id for confirmed no-op actions
open_points.text: Registry "mints a confirmation id when the owner confirms an action that asks for confirmation" and writes it into that action's audit entry, but archiving an already archived project and anonymising an already anonymised project return unchanged, while M09 records only significant changes of state.
open_points.question: When a confirmed action succeeds as an unchanged no-op, is a confirmation id minted, and is an audit entry created to retain it?
options: Mint an id and write a no-op audit entry
Mint no id and write no audit entry
Mint an id but do not retain it
open_points.default_guess: Mint no confirmation id and write no audit entry when validation determines that no state change occurs.

open_points.subject: Artifact owner service
open_points.text: A pointer carries "its type, one of the vocabulary the specification declares, and so its owner service, which the vocabulary fixes"; State 0 also says the pointer "names its owner service".
open_points.question: Is the owner service a fact stored on every ArtifactPointer, or only a value derived from its type's current vocabulary entry?
options: Store the owner service on the pointer
Derive it from the pointer type
Store it and require it always to equal the vocabulary
open_points.default_guess: Derive the owner service from the type vocabulary.

open_points.subject: Imported artifact pointer provenance and times
open_points.text: Every pointer must carry "the instant it was published and by which principal", a superseded instant when applicable, and "the instant it was withdrawn and by which principal"; the import rule only says that a source pointer keeps its published and superseded instants and is silent about principals and the withdrawn instant.
open_points.question: What facts are assigned to an imported pointer when the source does not supply the newly required publication or withdrawal principal or a required status-change instant?
options: Require every source pointer to supply all mandatory facts
Use the importing owner and import instant for missing facts
Represent unavailable legacy provenance or times explicitly
Refuse only pointers with missing facts
open_points.default_guess: Represent unavailable legacy provenance explicitly while preserving every source value that exists.

open_points.subject: Access-version movement
open_points.text: The access version is "an ordinal that every change of the granted set, the active project or the pending request moves"; one action can change more than one of those facts, such as revoking the active project or granting and making it active.
open_points.question: Does one atomic action that changes multiple access facts advance the access version once or once per changed fact?
options: Advance once per accepted action
Advance once per changed fact
Define separate versions for the components
open_points.default_guess: Advance once per accepted atomic action.

open_points.subject: AccessRequest value identity
open_points.text: The request carries "the instant it was made", but its identity evidence says a new request with the same text replaces the previous one and "nothing distinguishes the two".
open_points.question: Does the made instant participate in an AccessRequest value's identity/equality, making two equal-text requests distinct values, or is identity determined only by the text?
options: Text and made instant distinguish the value
Only the text determines value equality
AccessRequest has no equality beyond being the session's current pending value
open_points.default_guess: Treat each pending request as a whole value of text plus made instant, without giving it a separate identifier.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry identity
open_points.text: AuditEntry is classified as an entity and "two entries with equal facts are two events", but its complete fact list contains no audit-entry identity and the identity-format section declares none.
open_points.question: What makes two fact-for-fact equal AuditEntries distinct, and who creates that identity?
options: Registry mints an opaque audit-entry id
An append-stream position identifies the occurrence
The occurrence has hidden persistence identity but no domain identity fact
AuditEntry should be a value rather than an entity
open_points.default_guess: Use a Registry-minted opaque audit-entry id.

open_points.subject: Audit subject
open_points.text: The subject is defined as "the project (`project_id`) or the customer (`customer_ref`) changed" with a session-and-project variant for grants; the import later uses the migration closure as subject, and the entry created by erasing old audit entries has only the supplied date named.
open_points.question: What subject fact does each non-project/customer entry carry, especially the import entry and the audit-erasure entry?
options: Use a tagged subject union including project, customer, session-project, migration closure and audit log
Allow the subject to be absent for audit erasure
Use the confirmation id or supplied cutoff date as the audit-erasure subject
open_points.default_guess: Use a tagged subject union and an explicit audit-log subject for erasing old entries.

open_points.subject: Session removals caused by project erasure
open_points.text: M09 records both project anonymisation/deletion and revocation of a session's project, while R0-61 says project erasure automatically removes the project from every session; the text does not say whether those automatic removals produce additional revocation entries.
open_points.question: When project erasure removes grants from one or more sessions, does Registry write only the project-erasure entry or also one revocation entry for each affected session?
options: Write only the project-erasure entry
Also write one revocation entry per affected session
Write one project-erasure entry containing the affected session identities
open_points.default_guess: Write the project-erasure entry plus one revocation entry for each affected session.

open_points.subject: Imported-file digest
open_points.text: MigrationClosure carries "the identity of the file accepted, as a digest", but the text does not say whether Registry computes that digest or accepts it as a fact supplied with the import.
open_points.question: Who establishes the accepted file's digest fact?
options: Registry computes it from the accepted file
The import request supplies it and Registry stores it
The migration script supplies it and Registry verifies it
open_points.default_guess: Registry computes the digest from the file it actually accepts.

open_points.subject: Agent projection artifact pointers
open_points.text: The agent projection contains "artifact pointers" without saying whether that means every published, superseded and withdrawn pointer or only the currently published pointers.
open_points.question: Which ArtifactPointers does reading the agent projection return?
options: Every pointer in the project's history
Only currently published pointers
Only the latest published pointer of each type
open_points.default_guess: Return every pointer, matching the separately defined artifact-history read.
